## Proof

**Step 1 — Reformulation.** The Consistency Protocol says: in every triangle, if two edges share a color, the third does too. Equivalently, every triangle is either **monochromatic** (all three edges the same color) or **rainbow** (all three edges distinct colors).

**Step 2 — Each color gives an equivalence relation.** For each color $c\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, define $u\sim_c v$ iff $u=v$ or edge $uv$ has color $c$. This is an equivalence relation: transitivity holds because if $uv$ and $vw$ both have color $c$ (with $u,v,w$ distinct), then in triangle $uvw$ two edges share color $c$, forcing $uw$ to also have color $c$. So each color $c$ partitions the vertex set into **blocks**; intra-block edges are color $c$, inter-block edges are not. Since every edge has exactly one color, every pair of vertices lies in exactly one common block (across all 4 partitions).

**Step 3 — Every block has size $\le 3$.** Suppose color $c$ has a block $A$ with $|A|\ge 4$. Since all four colors are used, some edge is not color $c$, so some vertex $w$ lies outside $A$. For any distinct $u,v\in A$, triangle $uvw$ has $uv$ colored $c$ and $uw,vw$ colored $\ne c$. If $uw$ and $vw$ shared a color $c'$, then two edges would be color $c'$ while the third is $c\ne c'$—violating the protocol. So all edges from $w$ to $A$ must have pairwise distinct colors. But only 3 colors $\ne c$ exist while $|A|\ge 4$: pigeonhole contradiction. Hence $|A|\le 3$.

**Step 4 — Counting upper bound.** Each partition decomposes $[n]$ into blocks of size $\le 3$, so the number of edges of any one color is at most $3\lfloor n/3\rfloor + \binom{n\bmod 3}{2}$. Since the 4 partitions cover all $\binom{n}{2}$ edges exactly once:

$$\binom{n}{2}\le 4\!\left(3\Big\lfloor\frac{n}{3}\Big\rfloor+\binom{n\bmod 3}{2}\right).$$

For $n=10$: RHS $=4\cdot 9=36<45=\binom{10}{2}$. So $n\le 9$.

**Step 5 — Construction achieving $n=9$.** Use the affine plane $AG(2,3)$ over $\mathbb{F}_3$. The 9 points are $\mathbb{F}_3^2$. Its 12 lines partition into **4 parallel classes** (directions $(1\!:\!0),(0\!:\!1),(1\!:\!1),(1\!:\!2)$), each class being 3 disjoint triples covering all 9 points. Assign each parallel class a distinct color; color edge $uv$ by the class of the unique line through $u,v$.

- Every pair lies on exactly one line → every edge gets exactly one color. ✓
- Each class has 3 lines × 3 edges = 9 edges, so all 4 colors are active. ✓
- **Collinear triple** → all three edges on the same line → monochromatic. ✓
- **Non-collinear triple** → the three sides are three pairwise-intersecting lines, hence no two are parallel → three distinct parallel classes → rainbow. ✓

This satisfies the Consistency Protocol with $n=9$ and all four providers active.

**Conclusion.** The maximum possible number of islands is $\boxed{9}$.
